name: TinyDB
tagline: Pure-Python document store that keeps every table in one human-readable JSON file.
description: TinyDB is a small document-oriented database written in pure Python with no dependencies. Documents are plain dicts grouped into tables inside a single JSON file (or held in memory), and you query them with a Python Query DSL instead of SQL. It shines in scripts, CLI tools, prototypes and small desktop apps where SQLite feels heavy or a diffable text file is handy. The trade-off is deliberate: the whole file is read into memory, there are no indexes, no ACID guarantees and no safe access from multiple processes or threads. Release 4.9.0 (August 2026) is current and requires Python 3.10 or newer.

pricing.notes: Free on PyPI; no commercial edition.

scale.notes: Whole database lives in memory and is rewritten to disk on change; comfortable up to a few MB to tens of MB.

strengths: Zero dependencies and pure Python: pip install and go, on any platform CPython runs
Data sits in a single readable JSON file you can inspect, diff or commit to git
Pluggable storages and middlewares (e.g. in-memory storage, write caching) are easy to write
Tiny, fully tested codebase that is easy to read and extend
weaknesses: No indexes: every query scans all documents in the table
Entire database is loaded into memory and serialized on writes
Not safe for concurrent access from multiple processes or threads (e.g. a Flask app)
useCases: State and config storage for CLI tools and scripts
Small single-user desktop or hobby apps
Collecting small scraped or logged datasets
notIdealFor: Datasets larger than comfortably fit in RAM as JSON
Workloads needing indexes, joins or transactions
